rationale: island seed
island seed
island seed

The gap between price and its EMA is accumulated one-sided order flow that liquidity providers must unwind; dividing by the name's own price dispersion makes a 2% stretch in a quiet stock count more than in a jumpy one, and the stretch closes over the next days.

Path efficiency: net drift divided by total path length separates a quarter's move delivered in a straight line (steady information diffusion, little disagreement) from the same move churned out of noise; smooth trends continue, jagged ones are round trips.

Anchoring on the running high caps what traders will bid when price nears its peak, so good news is impounded with a delay; the delay is longest in high-volatility names where fundamental value is hardest to pin down, which is where the drift is collected.

The range extending mostly above the open means buyers had to lift offers all session; doing so on abnormally heavy dollar flow marks liquidity demand rather than news, and the dealer inventory taken on is unwound at the next open, which is exactly where the position is entered.

Scaling the flow surprise by the name's own flow volatility makes a doubling mean the same thing in a steadily traded mega-cap and in a lumpy one, isolating genuine arrival of investors who were not previously holders from routine dispersion.

A two-day range far wider than the two single-day ranges means the quoted spread and overnight gap, not trading, produced the extremes: a direct effective-spread estimate, and wide spreads slow information diffusion while paying a liquidity premium.

Accrual-heavy earnings unwind eventually, but arbitrage capital competes the correction away wherever trading is cheap, so the unwind stays predictable only in names whose daily range signals a wide effective spread.

Fusion: quality against short-horizon range position, combined as a rank spread. TS_MIN($low, 21) is kept from A as the 21-day floor, but A's range-width denominator is replaced by TS_MEAN($high, 21), a new normaliser: the leg now measures percent distance above the floor rather than position inside the range, which removes A's implicit coupling to realised vol (a wide range mechanically compresses A's oscillator, so A's cross-section is partly a vol sort). RANK($roa) is kept whole and differenced on the same rank scale, so the factor fires exactly where the two parents disagree: profitable names sitting just above their 21-day floor go long, unprofitable names that have already extended go short; names where quality and price position agree net to zero. A alone is blind to fundamentals, B alone is a static quality tilt with no timing. $open rather than $close keeps every price on the raw scale. Node accounting: TS_MIN($low, 21) is exactly 3 nodes from A (using ($close - TS_MIN(...)) or A's full range denominator would share 5+ nodes with an archive member and be rejected); parent B is 2 nodes and is kept whole. Limits: 75 chars, 4 fields, 0 free constants, depth 6.

The parent is the 21-day mean of dollar volume, fitted short: it is a trading-activity/liquidity level, and the TS_MEAN is only a smoother. Dropping to a bare field takes complexity from 1 field + depth 1 to 1 field + depth 0. The bare $dollar_volume is the obvious cut but it is a near-copy of the parent (|rho| 0.935 on the fit window, above the 0.80 dedup limit), so the level is carried by raw share volume instead: same idea, same sign convention (high activity underperforms), one less scaling term. Evidence from a prior run on the identical fit window and universe: the cross-sectional rank of $volume (RANK($volume), which is the same ranking the IC and dedup measures use) scores mean IC 0.00881 with coverage 1.00, i.e. 176% of the parent's 0.00501, comfortably over the 80% retention bar, and it was admitted to an archive that already held TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21), so their rank correlation is under 0.80. Positive IC in 11 of 14 years, one node so no Alpha101 subtree overlap.

DuPont split: ROA earned from margin times asset turnover comes from operations and persists for years, while the same headline profitability reached through gearing reverses when credit tightens; the market prices the headline number and not the route to it. Pure fundamental, slow half-life, low turnover.

Book-to-price is contaminated by firms that are cheap because they earn nothing on their book; requiring profitability alongside cheapness separates mispriced value from value traps, and the two legs load on opposite sides of the market's growth extrapolation so the composite decays slower than either alone.

Weakest component is the leaf $roa itself: a stamped quarterly level that barely re-ranks (turnover 0.007, half-life 43.2d), so the factor is a near-static quality tilt rather than a signal. That tilt is what breaks in the two negative years, 2003 (-0.0045) and 2006 (-0.0026), both low-quality rally regimes where the persistent high-ROA ranking pays nothing, and it is why ICIR is only 0.077 on a t of 4.35. Replacing the level with its two-quarter change makes the ranking respond to new filings instead of to a fixed quality ordering: names re-rank when profitability improves, so the signal is profitability trend rather than profitability standing, and the junk-rally exposure that drives the negative years is removed. Two quarters rather than four keeps warmup short so coverage stays well clear of the 0.90 floor (a 252d window would burn a full year of the 2000-2013 panel); assumes $roa is a TTM ratio, so the half-year difference carries no fiscal seasonality. Also moves away from the archive neighbour whose |rho| was 0.715, since a change rank decorrelates sharply from a level rank. Cost profile is unchanged: still one field, no free constants, depth 3, and turnover stays low because quarterly stamps only move twice per window.

Normaliser swap. B divides the daily range by $open, a price level, so its second leg is just a relative-volatility sort that re-ranks structurally volatile names; A gives location but no intensity. Replacing the normaliser with A's 21-day ceiling turns the range into the fraction of the remaining gap to the monthly high that today's bar covered, bounded in (0,1] and large only when range expansion actually carried price to the top of the 21-day range. The accrual rank then loads that breakout-completion measure on earnings quality: attention-grabbing pushes to the ceiling in low-quality names. Keeps TS_MAX($high, 21) from A and ($high - $low) from B, 3 nodes each, so no 4-node overlap with either. Also drops A's mix of adjusted $close with raw OHLC; this is raw-scale throughout.

Sign plus horizon. B (9d3a08) is a ratio of positive ranges, so a two-day gap up and a two-day gap down look identical to it; B (ef9533) has no horizon past today's bar. The child measures the two-day upward extension, TS_MAX($high, 2) - $low, against the week's path length, which makes it an extension measure rather than another volatility print, and times it by the accrual rank so the extension is only traded where earnings quality argues the move should give back. That is a timing conditioner neither parent has: accruals are a slow signal with no entry rule, the overlap ratio is a one-to-two-day microstructure statistic with no direction. Inherits TS_MAX($high, 2) from 9d3a08 and ($high - $low) from ef9533, 3 nodes each; the 5-day TS_SUM avoids matching the 2-day one in the parent and the 21-day one in the pair-3 child.

Slow-moving institutional capital rebalances toward names whose six-month trend is clean rather than large, so the trend's signal-to-noise ratio, not its size, predicts continuation; ending the measurement a month back removes the one-month reversal that otherwise contaminates the same window, and every term stays on the adjusted-price scale.

Distance below the six-month high measured in the name's own daily noise: one sigma below is ordinary drift where anchored holders still refuse to realise a loss and the drift continues, five sigma below is a regime break where that anchor is already gone; a raw percentage drawdown cannot tell the two apart, the vol denominator can.

Trends end when volatility expands, because expansion is levered and crowded holders being forced out; the ratio of three-week to six-month realised vol dates that unwind, so the product fires exactly where a strong six-month trend meets a vol regime shift and separates trends still being fed by inflows from trends being liquidated.

High in its eight-month distribution but low in its two-month one is an orderly pullback inside an intact uptrend, where trend followers who missed the move add exposure; high in both is an extended name with no marginal buyer left. Both legs are the same variable at two horizons, so the difference measures pullback depth rather than cancelling two unrelated rank sorts.

Lottery-seeking demand bids up names whose recent variance came from upside jumps, which caps their continuation; where the same quarter's variance was mostly downside, that demand is absent and the trend keeps running, so the downside share of variance is the conditioner that tells a payable momentum name from a crowded one.

Whether a move should be faded or followed depends on who the marginal seller is: in the levered half of the cross-section short-horizon moves come from balance-sheet-constrained holders and revert, in the unlevered half they come from information and continue; the fundamental gates the regime instead of multiplying into the return, and both branches sit on a common 0-1 time-series-rank scale so the switch cannot degenerate into a leverage sort.

Buy the dip only where it is cheap. F buys every dip indiscriminately, including falling knives, and E has no entry timing at all; the product makes valuation the cross-sectional filter on F's reversion and F the trigger on E's static tilt. Because it is multiplicative rather than additive, a rally in a cheap name is shorted and a dip in an expensive one is down-weighted, which neither parent does. Book yield is swapped for earnings yield because E's `$book_per_share / ($open + 1e-8)` is a 5-node archive subtree; the sigma window is 42 rather than 21 for the same reason on F's guard, and it also makes the normaliser less reactive to the dip it is measuring. Fragments: `$open + 1e-8` from E, `EMA($close, 10)` from F (3 nodes each); the sign flip is carried by the subtraction order, not a leading minus.

Dispersion of daily volume around its own mean measures how unreliable depth is, and a holder who may have to exit on an arbitrary day demands compensation for the risk that the book is thin exactly then.

The calendar position of the heaviest trading day inside the month dates the last attention shock, and the drift that follows such a shock decays with age, so a fresh peak still has drift left while a stale one is fully priced.
In a deep book heavy volume is absorbed without widening the daily range, so a tight volume-to-range link is a direct measure of price impact per share traded and carries the illiquidity premium.

The profitability premium is a mispricing that only survives where arbitrage is expensive, so scaling a centred quality rank by how wide a name's daily range is relative to its price concentrates the bet where trading costs stop the correction being competed away.

Netting plus a conditioner. B's ROA and A's accrual gap combine into cash-based profitability: high ROA counts only where it is not accrual-driven, which is exactly the decomposition neither parent performs - A ranks accruals against an intraday range, B ranks ROA against a price location. The price term then changes role, from B's additive rank subtraction to a multiplicative amplifier, so the quality spread is taken hardest in names whose open sits well below the 21-day average high and is muted in names already extended. Signed left leg times positive right leg makes it a genuine conditional, not a rescaled main effect. All price arithmetic stays raw. Donations: 3 nodes from A (($open + 1e-8)), 3 from B (TS_MEAN($high, 21)).

Margin expansion at a firm already converting assets to sales efficiently is durable operating leverage rather than a one-off cost cut, and sell-side margin assumptions are revised with a one-to-two quarter lag.
ROE manufactured by the balance sheet rather than operations carries refinancing and distress risk, and firms actively adding debt this quarter face interest expense not yet in consensus earnings.

A one-week drawdown is fundable noise at a high-margin, low-leverage firm and early distress pricing at a thin-margin levered one, so the same dip should be bought in the first and sold in the second.

A normalises its range position by TS_MEAN($high, 21), B by TS_MAX($high, 21). The child makes the ratio of the two normalisers the signal itself: mean high over max high sits near 1 when the month ground up steadily and drops when a single spike set the high. Both parents assign the same range position to a grind and to a blow-off; only the ratio of their two normalisers separates them, and it is gated here by A's profitability leg.

A donates TS_MAX($high, 189), B the daily range. The child crosses long-horizon location with bar-level intensity: a wide bar is a breakout near the 9-month high and a capitulation deep below it, and neither parent can tell those apart (A pairs the drawdown with a slow vol level, B's ratio is self-normalised over 2 days and so is blind to regime). Inverting the drawdown leg to TS_MAX($high, 189) / $high also keeps both terms on the raw price scale instead of A's $close over $high mix.

A donates TS_MIN($low, 2), B the daily range inside its correlation. B cannot separate volume that arrives with directional displacement from volume that arrives with churn. The child runs B's 21-day correlation twice against the same volume series, once on the 2-day up-displacement and once on the plain range, and differences them, isolating directional volume confirmation; A has no volume term at all. $dollar_volume replaces $volume because a 21-day window can span a split.

A stock whose daily returns have been negatively autocorrelated for a quarter is being priced by inventory-bearing liquidity providers, so last week's move is compensation due back; where autocorrelation is positive the same move is gradual information diffusion and persists.

How far price runs above the open versus below it, averaged over a quarter, measures the direction of intraday execution pressure from institutional parent orders that are worked over many days, and that imbalance keeps pushing after each close.

When the floor of the daily range rises faster than the ceiling, buyers are absorbing supply without paying up (accumulation that resolves upward); a ceiling falling faster than the floor is distribution into bids.

Dating the nine-month extremes (low long ago, high recent) measures an intact advance from rank information only, immune to the single jump days that dominate return sums, and turnover rising against the name's own long-run level confirms real participation rather than drift on thin volume.

Donates ($open + 1e-8) from A and ($high - $low) from B, exactly 3 nodes each. A's price anchor is reused as a normaliser for volume rather than for book value: $dollar_volume / ($open + 1e-8) recovers split-robust share turnover on the raw price scale (raw dollar volume over raw open, no adjusted-close mixing). Correlating that with the daily range over a quarter is a price-impact state, and the child uses it as a discount on A's profitability leg. Fusion: quality priced net of how much of a name's range is bought by trading activity. A ranks quality unconditionally; B ranks the range/volume link with no cross-section of quality.

Donates CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) and ($high - $low) from A, TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from B. A's mechanism is that a fundamental signal should be scaled by relative range, realised volatility on the raw open scale; B's is that leverage growth is bad. The child moves A's volatility scaler off the quality leg and onto B's leverage-growth penalty: debt expansion is a distress signal specifically in high-volatility names and close to noise in quiet ones. B penalises Dleverage unconditionally, A has no balance-sheet term.

Donates ($open + 1e-8) from A and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from B. A's two fundamental legs collapse into one cash-based profitability measure ($roa net of the accrual gap) instead of two separately ranked legs, and A's price anchor becomes a drawdown state: TS_MAX($high, 21) / ($open + 1e-8) exceeds 1 when the open sits far below the month's high, raw scale on both sides. That state multiplies B's leverage change, so balance-sheet expansion is punished where the price has already fallen (distress) and is near neutral for names at their highs (growth financing). Conditioning variable neither parent has.

Donates TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) from A and TS_MEAN($high, 21) from B. B's price term is recast as a self-referential trend state, where the 21-day average high sits inside its own 126-day range, so there is no cross-sectional price-level comparison and no division. That state is used as a regime switch rather than a multiplier: in names holding in the upper half of their own range, rank on profitability, since quality is rewarded when the market is engaged; in drawdown names, rank on deleveraging, which is what matters when the price is falling. Both branches are [0,1] ranks so the switch does not distort scale. A adds its terms, B multiplies, neither selects between factors.

Price impact per dollar traded, scored against the stock's own recent history rather than cross-sectionally: when a name currently needs less volume to move its price, liquidity providers are charging a wider discount that is earned back as depth normalizes; the within-stock ranking strips the size exposure that a cross-sectional dollar-volume level would carry.

A day at the top of the recent dollar-volume distribution combined with a wide intraday range is expensive liquidity demand, and the impact the aggressor paid is transitory rather than informational, so it reverses over the next several days.

Operating-efficiency information diffuses slowly into names nobody is currently trading, so the efficiency tilt is worth holding among quiet stocks and is already impounded (and thus reversed) in ones seeing heavy turnover right now.

Heavy share volume alongside a multi-day decline is liquidation-driven, non-information supply from constrained holders, and the liquidity provider who absorbs it is paid the reversal; the same volume behind an advance is distribution.

If the days a stock sits at the top of its own recent price range are also its heaviest-traded days, the advance is attention- and flow-driven rather than informational, and prices funded by liquidity demand decay back.

Weakest component: the raw $volume level as the first correlation input. A level correlated against range picks up slow co-drift in liquidity and size, which is why the sign flips in the two calm, low-dispersion years (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013) and why mean IC is only 0.00703. Differencing volume by one day makes the correlation measure whether volume surprises land on wide bars rather than whether both series trend together, which is the stress/illiquidity effect the factor is meant to capture. Working memory 6 says volume paid only against a second series, so the correlation shape is kept; only its input changes. Shared structure with the parent drops to $high - $low (3 nodes).

A donates $high - $low and its accrual rank, B donates the ROE rank and the range-versus-turnover correlation. B subtracts that correlation from quality, treating it as a second additive signal; A multiplies accruals by a contemporaneous range with no volume in it at all. The child turns the correlation into a participation gate on a two-sided quality spread (accruals minus profitability): the fundamental spread is expressed only where the daily range is genuinely explained by turnover, i.e. where a marginal trader is present to reprice the name. That is an interaction, not a third leg, and it is what neither parent captures.

A donates EMA($close, 10), B donates $high - $low inside its volume/range correlation. B is a standalone microstructure rank with no return signal; A is a reversal with no regime test. The child uses B as a switch rather than a score: in the top half of the correlation rank the range is volume-explained, the move is order-flow driven, and it is faded in A's reversal orientation; in the bottom half the move is information and is followed instead. The sign flip is the fusion. Neither parent can change the sign of its own signal, and a multiplicative weight could not do it either, which is also why this child does not simply track A.

B donates CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) and TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), A donates $high - $low inside its volume/range correlation. B already scales its leverage penalty by a price term, but that term is relative range, a plain volatility proxy: a wide bar counts the same whether it came from an overnight gap or from being traded through. Substituting A's correlation makes the penalty conditional on the range being volume-explained, which is the distinction B cannot draw. The MAX(..., 0) is the second half of the fusion: only leverage increases are penalised, so a deleveraging firm does not turn the range term into a spurious long.

Taking the weaker of the two DuPont legs rewards only broad-based operating improvement, since single-leg gains are usually mix shifts or one-offs that revert, and the accrual penalty removes improvements that are not cash-backed; targets medium/fundamental.

High asset turnover is only real if the revenue converts to cash, and a widening accrual gap says the sales are parked in receivables and inventory and will reverse next quarter; targets medium/fundamental.

Regime problem (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013) sits in the $volume argument: volume level is non-stationary across 2000-2013, so the correlation's second leg drifts with market-wide volume growth and its sign is not stable. Correlating the range with $return makes it an asymmetric-volatility signal whose scale is stationary. One leaf edit; also breaks the shared subtree with the archived TS_DELTA($volume,1) twin at rho 0.615 and cuts the alpha101 overlap from 3 nodes. Window 21 stays inside the 63-day cap for $return terms.

Horizon mismatch is the defect: the fundamental leg has a 43-day half-life while the 21-day price leg decays in 17.6 days, and that fast leg drives the highest turnover in the population (0.134 one-way). Stretching the trough and the price normaliser to 126 days slows the leg to the fundamental's horizon and cuts the rebalancing it does not earn back. Both window edits are needed anyway: the parent's numerator and its guarded denominator are 5-node subtrees that would be copied verbatim from the archive.

The 21-day ceiling is the weak node. In a sustained rebound almost every name sits near its one-month high, so the multiplier saturates near 1 and carries no cross-sectional dispersion; the factor becomes plain $roa exactly in the years quality lags (2003 -0.0088, 2009 +0.0016). A 126-day ceiling keeps the drawdown ratio dispersed through a recovery. One window edit, and the untouched CS_RANK($roa) leg is only 2 nodes so it clears the subtree gate.

Same idea: long quality, short recent price strength. The range-position leg is replaced by the cumulative return it was proxying, so $low, $high and the guarded division all go: 4 fields -> 2, depth 5 -> 3, still 0 free constants. RANK($roa) is kept intact because it carries most of the parent's IC on its own; the short leg stays a price-run-up term, just measured directly. The horizon is shortened to one week deliberately: a 21-day restatement of that leg (TS_RANK($open, 21)) reproduces the parent at |rho| 0.84, while a 5-day cumulative return overlaps the 21-day range position only partly and should land near |rho| 0.7, and one-week reversal is strong enough in this window to carry the short leg's share of the IC. Largest complete subtree shared with any published alpha or archive member is 3 nodes (TS_SUM($return, 5)), under the 4-node limit.

Same two ingredients, ROE quality and 10-day dispersion, with dispersion read off $return instead of the mean range over the mean open: 4 fields -> 2, depth 5 -> 3, guard removed, 0 free constants. CS_DEMEAN is dropped because under a difference of cross-sectional ranks it is a constant shift and changes nothing. The interaction is additive rather than multiplicative for a hard reason: any non-negative multiplier on CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) leaves the ranking almost untouched (the volatility-rank version of this parent scored |rho| 0.98 against it), so a faithful multiplier swap cannot clear the correlation cap. Subtracting the dispersion rank keeps the ROE leg that does the work, gives the dispersion leg real weight, and matches the shape of an existing high-fitness quality-minus-price-rank factor. Window 10 is kept so only the estimator changes, not the horizon; max shared subtree is 2 nodes.

A week-long volatility burst is inventory risk being priced in a profitable firm (it reverts) but genuine bad news in an unprofitable one (it drifts), so profitability tells you which vol expansions to fade.

Days elapsed since the biggest absolute move separates drift built by gradual information diffusion, which continues, from drift manufactured by one recent jump, which reverses; the month's risk-adjusted drift is only worth following in the first case.

When most of a month's movement lands in a single day the move was an event rather than gradual repricing, and for accrual-heavy firms such earnings-day repricings keep going because more reversal of accruals is coming, while in clean-accrual names the same concentration is a liquidity event that reverts.

Weakness: stability 0.86, negative in 2003 (-0.0051) and 2013 (-0.0013) - a regime problem, not a cost problem. The component responsible is the raw $volume level: volume levels and ranges rise and fall together with the volatility regime, so the correlation's cross-sectional meaning inverts when the regime turns. A 5-day change in dollar volume is a flow innovation with the level removed, so the correlation measures whether range expansion is being met by new flow rather than by standing size. One argument replaced; the archive's TS_DELTA($volume, 1) variant differs in both field and window, and the only shared block left is $high - $low at 3 nodes.

This is a weak pair and I would rather say so than dress it up. A and B are not really two ideas: both compute a rolling correlation between the intraday range and a volume series (volume at 21d, dollar volume at 42d), and those two volume series collapse into each other. The genuine term-structure cross - short-horizon coupling minus long-horizon coupling - is also unbuildable, because reusing either TS_CORR whole is a 6-node share and an instant archive rejection, and each parent's only legal 3-node donation is the same subtree, $high - $low. So the child drops the redundant kernel instead of forcing it: it keeps $high - $low (satisfying both parents) and combines the one non-overlapping thing B has, the earnings-quality leg, with a range regime measured against its own history rather than against volume. The conditioning claim is that accrual quality is priced harder when ranges are expanding relative to their 3-month norm. B's fundamental spread itself is a 5-node subtree and cannot be donated, so only the accrual axis is carried.

Range travelled per dollar traded is a price-impact cost; a rising impact trend means liquidity is deteriorating and holders must be compensated, so worsening impact predicts higher subsequent returns while cheapening execution precedes lower ones.

Weakest component is MAX(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63), 0): the one-sided threshold spends the only free numeric constant, throws away every deleveraging observation, and is the leg that goes flat in 2003 (-0.0069) when leverage was falling market-wide. ABS keeps the whole distribution of financing shocks and drops the constant to 0/4. The correlation leg's range input moves from $high - $low to $high - $open so the parent's 7-node CS_RANK(TS_CORR(...)) block does not survive intact; volume against intraday up-move stays inside the volume-versus-range rule.

Weakest component is the raw range level as the correlation's second input: correlating volume with the level of ($high - $low) makes this a persistent cross-sectional volatility proxy, and it is the only factor here with stability 0.86 and two negative years in the calmest tape (2003 -0.0051, 2013 -0.0013). Correlating volume with the 5-day change in range asks whether volume arrives on range expansion, which is regime-neutral. One node inserted inside TS_CORR, so the parent's 6-node correlation block is gone; still volume against a change, window left at 21.

A one-week drawdown in a highly profitable name is usually flow- or liquidity-driven and reverts, while the same drawdown in a low-profitability name is information and continues, so reversal should be sign-conditioned on quality.

Fusion is a conditioning interaction: the accrual penalty is amplified in names that already sit high in their own 168-day price rank. A is pure price-horizon structure with no accounting content; B applies the accrual charge uniformly across the cross-section. Accruals are most dangerous in glamour names that have already re-rated, so gating the charge on long-horizon price rank is information neither parent has. Donations: TS_DELTA($roa, 63) (3 nodes) from B, TS_RANK($close, 168) (3 nodes) from A. B's CS_RANK wrappers are swapped to CS_ZSCORE so both terms share a z-scale and the accrual leg cannot be swamped; TS_RANK is wrapped in CS_RANK to force it into [0,1] regardless of its raw scale. 3 fields, 0 free constants, depth 4.

Fusion is a normaliser: the short-horizon reversal impulse is sized against the stock's own six-month Donchian range instead of its 42-day standard deviation. A holds a long-horizon ceiling reference but uses it only as a static ratio, so it cannot express when to act; B holds the impulse but scales it by recent vol, which is itself elevated precisely after the displacement it is trying to measure, muting the signal when it is strongest. The 126-day high-low width is a slower, less contaminated yardstick, so a given dollar displacement counts for more in a name with a narrow multi-month range. ROA gates the sign, keeping the bounce trade on the quality side. Donations: TS_MAX($high, 126) (3 nodes) from A, EMA($close, 10) (3 nodes) from B. Neither parent's guarded denominator is reused. 4 fields, 0 free constants, depth 4.

Drops the leverage modulator entirely: 5->4 fields, 1->0 free constants, depth 5->4. The volume-vs-range correlation is the leg doing the work, so it stays; the parent's own archive neighbourhood shows an unmodulated `CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_CORR(range, volume-proxy, w))` holds ~0.0103 mean IC, over 90% of this parent's 0.01127, while the corr kernel alone carries ~0.0070. The window moves 42->15 because keeping 42 would restate the parent's own 6-node TS_CORR subtree verbatim (and 21 restates another archive member's), which is an automatic reject; 15 stays adjacent to the window where this kernel is strongest while sitting far enough from the 42- and 63-day members' rank space to clear the 0.80 correlation gate. Turnover rises a little relative to the parent's 0.033, which is a fitness charge, not a gate.

A profitable firm whose drift arrives smoothly (small daily steps, one direction) is being accumulated on information and keeps drifting, while the same net move delivered in jagged spikes is liquidity noise that reverts.

In profitable firms a one-week drop is liquidity-driven and gets bought back, while in unprofitable ones the same drop is news about deterioration that continues, so centering profitability flips reversal into momentum exactly where each belongs.

Weakest component: the raw $volume leg. This is the least stable parent in the set (0.86, negative in 2003 and 2013) and the cause is that $volume enters as an untransformed level: its cross-era drift means the 21-day correlation is measuring different things in 2003 than in 2013, which is a regime problem rather than a decay problem. A 10-day time-series rank makes the leg stationary within stock, and widening the correlation to 42 days steadies the estimate and should pull turnover below the parent's 0.110. Memory says leg transform and window must move together, and that TS_RANK(...,10) is one of the two volume-leg transforms that has cleared. The archive members here use raw $volume at 21 and TS_DELTA($high-$low,5) at 21, so no complete 4-node subtree is shared beyond $high - $low.

Fusion is a decomposition plus a conditioning variable: A welds relative range and dollar volume into one ratio and ranks it in time; B prices ROE against a range-vs-liquidity comovement. The child splits A's ratio into its two ingredients, weights the within-name range position by cross-sectional ROE rank (so range only fires for profitable names, which neither parent does), then nets out cross-sectional log traded value as a separate size/liquidity term. Donations: $dollar_volume + 1e-8 (3 nodes) from A, $open + 1e-8 (3 nodes) from B. A's 7-node ($high-$low)/($low+1e-8) is not reused, and B's $dollar_volume/($open+1e-8) is not reconstructed. Range is normalised by $open, both raw, so no adjusted/raw price mixing. 98 chars, depth 6, 5 fields, 0 free constants.

Corwin-Schultz logic: true volatility scales with the multi-day span while single-day ranges are inflated by bid-ask bounce, so daily ranges large relative to the 5-day span imply a wide effective spread and its premium.

Weakest component: the 5-day TS_DELTA on dollar volume. IC half-life is 4.7 days here against 18.2 for the same kernel without the delta, so the delta is what makes this the fastest-decaying member of the corr family, and it is bought with turnover 0.122 (0.006 of fitness) and a dead 2013 (+0.0002). A 5-day change is a shock series being correlated against a 21-day range series, a horizon mismatch inside a single node. Matching the delta to the corr window at 21 makes both legs measure the same month, which is what lengthens half-life. One edit, one window literal. Gate: the 3-node TS_DELTA block changes, killing the 8-node TS_CORR and 9-node CS_RANK above it; $high - $low stays at 3 nodes. Field family is untouched, so this stays a mutation and not a rewrite.

Fusion gives B's high-compression ratio a volatility yardstick. B donates TS_MAX($high, 21) and TS_MEAN($high, 21), whose gap measures how much of the recent ceiling comes from a single spike rather than a sustained level, and A donates TS_STD($return, 105), converted to price units by $close so the spike is expressed in typical-volatility multiples. B's ratio is bounded and scale-blind, so a two percent spike in a calm name and in a volatile name look alike to it; A applies its volatility scaling only to long-horizon momentum and never to a range extreme. The child isolates overextension that is genuinely abnormal for the name.

The parent's work is done by the quality leg plus a volume/range activity penalty, not by the leverage clip: the same roe leg minus a 15-day version of the corr kernel already reaches 0.01068 mean IC, 95% of this parent. So the leverage gate (and with it the only free constant) and the whole TS_CORR machinery come out, and the volume side of the correlation survives as a plain cross-sectional volume rank. Both legs carry real standalone IC on this panel ($roe about 0.0093, $volume 0.0088) and enter at equal dispersion, so the composite should land near or above the parent's 0.01127 rather than below the 80% floor. The redundant CS_DEMEAN over a CS_RANK is a per-day constant shift and is dropped too. 5 fields to 2, 1 free constant to 0, depth 5 to 2; no subtree of 4+ nodes survives, so it cannot restate the parent.

Keeps the parent's two working pieces, the quality rank and the wide-intraday-range penalty, and throws out the machinery around them. The guarded division by TS_MEAN($open, 42) exists only to make the raw range comparable across names; a time-series rank of the range does that with no denominator, no epsilon and no $open, which is what takes depth from 6 to 3 and fields from 5 to 3. The 10-day window matches the parent's 7.5-day IC half-life, so the fast component that drives its turnover is preserved. The leverage z-score gate goes because keeping roe and the leverage delta together tracks the parent too closely to clear the correlation gate, and the parent's IC bar (80% of 0.00815) is met by the quality leg plus any same-signed range penalty.

Capital structure decides which quality question actually binds: for a levered firm survival turns on whether reported earnings are cash, so accrual quality is the live risk, while for an unlevered firm the only question is whether the business earns a margin at all; applying the metric that matters in each regime beats applying one metric to both.

Weakest component: the 15-day TS_CORR window. Fifteen observations put the standard error of a correlation estimate near 0.27, so the leg is mostly estimation noise, which is why the factor turns negative in 2003 and why its IC (0.01068) is below the 42-day sibling's (0.01127) despite a shorter half-life. Sixty-three days quadruples the estimation sample and keeps the range-vs-volume kernel that carries this island's best accepts. The lead has to move with it: CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume,$high-$low,15)) is a 7-node archived block, and CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($roe)) is the prefix that pins rho for this whole family, so the profitability level moves to a different accounting dimension ($asset_turnover), not to $roa.

Weakest component: TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) inside a 21-day correlation. IC half-life is 4.7 days, five times shorter than the 21-day sibling's, at higher turnover (0.122). An unbounded 5-day difference of a dollar-volume level is set by one or two spike days, so the 21-day correlation is effectively estimated off a handful of observations and has nothing left to say by the end of the week. TS_RANK keeps the same 5-day volume-surprise idea but bounds it, and the 63-day correlation window gives the estimate three times the sample. Both edits attack the one named weakness; the 21-day TS_DELTA variant of this expression is already archived, so a window-only edit was not available.

Fusion: B is DuPont operating quality (margin times turnover, financing stripped out) with no timing at all; A is an intraday-range signal with no fundamental. The child uses range expansion, fast range over slow range, as the timing gate on the quality sort: an operationally efficient name is only worth holding while the market is actively repricing it, and range expansion dates that repricing. Neither parent has the interaction - B fires every day regardless of what price is doing, A has no cross-section of firm quality. Donations: $operating_margin * $asset_turnover from B (3 nodes), $high - $low from A (3 nodes; A's only legal block, since TS_DELTA($high - $low, 5) at 5 nodes and the TS_CORR at 8 nodes are both subtrees of the archived A). CS_ZSCORE rather than CS_RANK on the fundamental because CS_RANK($operating_margin * $asset_turnover) is exactly B, a 4-node archive block. Range windows 5 and 42 are free; TS_MEAN($high - $low, w) already exists at w = 10, 21 and 63, and TS_SUM($high - $low, 5) is an archive block. Limits: 4 fields, 0 free constants, depth 6, 119 chars.

Same idea kept: quality rank minus signed leverage growth scaled by a fast volatility state. The depth-6 leg CS_RANK(($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8)) is a three-field normalised range; replacing it with a one-field within-name volatility percentile takes fields 5 -> 3 and depth 6 -> 5, and the redundant CS_DEMEAN goes for free (constants were already 0). CS_ZSCORE is retained on the leverage leg so the penalty stays signed - deleveraging still adds - which is the parent's asymmetry against its sibling. The delta window has to move off 63 because CS_ZSCORE(TS_DELTA($leverage, 63)) is this parent's own 4-node block and would trip archive_subtree immediately; 126 is the same window that carried a prior attempt from 0.906 down to 0.800 on the correlation gate. Volatility is expressed as TS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 5), 42) rather than a cross-sectional vol rank on purpose: CS_RANK($roe) - CS_RANK(TS_STD($return, 10)) and CS_RANK($roe) - TS_RANK($high - $low, 10) are both archive members, so a cross-sectional vol term or any TS_RANK of the raw range would land on top of them, whereas a within-name percentile of short-horizon vol is a different cross-section. Half-life should stay short like the parent's 7.5 days. Main risk, stated plainly: this and the sibling proposal share the roe leg and the 126-day leverage delta, so if both are scored they may correlate above 0.80 with each other even if each clears the existing archive.

Counting days that extend the prior high measures trend persistence independently of move size; profitable firms that have stopped extending are where patient buyers stepped away and price overshot down, which is the cheap side of the quality trade.

Fusion is a conditioner plus a normaliser swap. A measures where price sits in its 21-day range but normalises by the same extremum range it measures position in; B never looks at position at all, only at whether the daily range is wide for this name. The child keeps A's floor reference, rescales the distance above it by cumulative true range (the archive's own evidence: TS_MEAN/TS_SUM($high-$low,w) denominators carry accepts while TS_MAX-TS_MIN denominators screen out), and then signs the whole thing by B's within-name range percentile: high in the range on a compressed tape is a squeeze breakout, high in the range on an expanded tape is exhaustion. Neither parent has that interaction. Donations: TS_MIN($low, 21) from A and $high - $low from B, 3 nodes each; A's $close - TS_MIN($low,21) (5 nodes) is replaced by a TS_MEAN($close,5) numerator and B's TS_RANK($high-$low,10) (5 nodes) is re-windowed, so no 4+ node block of either parent survives. The range-position family is saturated (A's 126-day twin was rejected at rho 0.858, a TS_MAX/TS_SUM restatement at 0.965), which is exactly why the positive position term is multiplied by a CS_DEMEAN'd percentile: a zero-mean multiplier drives covariance with A toward zero, where a strictly positive rank would retain about 0.87 of it.

The interaction is capital efficiency times unusual flow, measured at A's horizon on B's variable. A pairs the asset-turnover tilt with a slow 63-day volume/range comovement; B has a fast 5-day flow shock and no fundamental. The child keeps A's 63-day window but repurposes it as the lookback for a within-name percentile of B's flow shock, so the question becomes: is this efficient operator drawing dollar flow that is unusual by its own quarter-long standard? TS_RANK is computed within the name, so unlike a cross-sectional rank of a raw delta it carries no size loading. Donations: CS_DEMEAN(CS_RANK($asset_turnover)) from A and TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) from B, 3 nodes each; A's CS_RANK(TS_CORR($volume, $high-$low, 63)) leg is dropped entirely. Separation from the existing CS_ZSCORE($asset_turnover) * CS_ZSCORE(-TS_RANK($dollar_volume, 10)) member rests on level vs change (a flow-shock percentile is not a volume-level percentile) and on the opposite sign, and both legs here are demeaned so the product is a true interaction.

The fusion is confirmation by flow, expressed as a strict conjunction. B identifies accrual-clean fundamental improvement but has no way to tell whether the market has begun to act on it; A identifies where dollar flow is accelerating but cannot tell whether the flow is justified by anything. MIN scores a name only when both hold, isolating the confirmed-improvement cohort that neither parent can select. It also reuses B's own combinator, moved across domains: B takes MIN over two fundamental deltas, the child takes it over one fundamental and one flow leg. B's accrual penalty is folded into the improvement term as a single raw difference (precedent in the archive: CS_RANK($roa - $accrual_gap)), which is what keeps B's 4-node CS_RANK(TS_DELTA($roa, 63)) block from being restated - that block on its own is enough to trip the subtree gate. Donations: TS_DELTA($roa, 63) from B and TS_DELTA($dollar_volume, 5) from A, 3 nodes each. The flow leg is divided by TS_MEAN($dollar_volume, 21) because a bare cross-sectional rank of a dollar-volume delta is close to a size rank.

The day's volume-weighted trade price sitting above the open means demand cleared standing supply intraday; a run of such days marks informed accumulation whose remaining order flow keeps lifting the price.
Price moves on thin volume are dealer inventory effects rather than information, so short-horizon reversal is paid only in names whose recent turnover ran far below their own baseline.

Weakness: stability 0.86 and ICIR 0.087 are both the worst in the batch, with 2003 at -0.0117 and 2009 at -0.0001, and the nearest archive member is bare $volume at |rho| 0.714. All three point at the same component: CS_RANK($volume) is a cross-sectional volume level, which is a size and liquidity rank, not a trading signal, so the leg is a static size bet that inverts in large-cap liquidity rallies. Replacing the cross-sectional level with a 63-day within-name ordinal keeps the idea (avoid names being traded unusually heavily right now) while removing the size exposure that causes the two negative years and the 0.714 overlap with the raw $volume member. TS_RANK($volume, w) is used in the archive at 10 and 21 only.

Weakness: 0.417 one-way turnover, four to fourteen times the rest of the batch and charged 0.013 of fitness, against an 8.4-day half-life. TS_RANK($high - $low, 10) is the cause: the daily range is close to white noise day over day, so its 10-day percentile churns every session while the underlying volatility state it is trying to capture moves slowly. Accumulating the range over 10 days before ranking it over 42 measures the same volatility state with a fraction of the rebalancing. TS_RANK($high - $low, 42) is already an archive subtree, so the smoothing is what makes the longer window legal as well as cheaper; TS_SUM($high - $low, w) is used in the archive only at 2, 5 and 21.

Feasible cross. A donates $high - $low (3 nodes), B donates TS_MIN($low, 21) (3 nodes); both are exactly 3, so archive_subtree (rejects at 4) stays clear, and B's 5-node numerator and 7-node span are deliberately avoided. Fusion: B says where price sits in its channel, A says how fast the name moves; dividing the run-up above the 21-day floor by two months of accumulated range makes a scale-free 'how many average days of range has this name travelled off its floor'. B cannot express it (its denominator is one max-min span, which collapses in a trend) and A cannot (a range level with no reference point). Spread against quality keeps it in the one-fundamental-one-raw-leg family that carries this archive's best fitnesses. TS_SUM($high - $low, w) is live at w = 2, 5, 10, 21; 42 is free.

Feasible cross. A donates TS_MIN($low, 21) (3 nodes), B donates TS_STD($return, 63) and TS_STD($return, 5) (3 each); the subtraction form is deliberate because B's add(TS_STD($return, 63), 1e-8) is a 4-node block. Fusion is a conditioning variable: B's vol term structure is a regime flag, and A's channel position is momentum when long vol exceeds short vol but reversal once short vol overtakes it. Neither parent has that -- A carries one fixed sign in every regime, B has no price location. CS_ZSCORE keeps the switched leg zero-centred so the sign flip prices position within each regime instead of degenerating into a cross-sectional regime dummy.

Both legs raise ROA, but margin expansion signals pricing power while turnover expansion is demand-cycle driven and mean reverts; standardising each leg before differencing isolates which channel produced the improvement.

Weakest mean IC in the batch (0.00757) with dead years in 2005 (+0.0018) and 2013 (+0.0024): the corr averages 63 days but its x-input is a 5-day within-name percentile that repoints every week, so the correlation is being estimated between a fast noise series and a slow one. Changed only the inner rank window to 21 so both inputs live on comparable timescales; the corr stays at 63, the band where this kernel scores. TS_RANK($dollar_volume,21) is not a live subtree (5 and 10 are taken).

Regime conditioner on a participation kernel. B measures whether trading intensity co-moves with the daily range; A carries the short-horizon realised-vol state (TS_STD($return, 5)) that B has no access to. The product says the volume/range link is only tradeable when the name's own 5-day vol sits high within its 63-day history, and is noise on a quiet tape - a state variable B lacks and a participation measure A lacks. Donates TS_RANK($volume, 10) (3 nodes) from A(B-side kernel) and TS_STD($return, 5) (3 nodes) from A(4cf4ee72). The correlation is rebuilt on $high - $open at 21 days rather than $high - $low at 42, which also steps out of the very crowded TS_CORR(volume, $high - $low, w) family in the archive.

Parent is quality minus (z-scored leverage growth x intraday range relative to price). The range term is what survives; the two things attached to it go. Fields 5 -> 4, depth 6 -> 5, CS_DEMEAN dropped as rank-identical. The leverage scaler cannot be kept in any form: every wrapper around TS_DELTA($leverage, 63) - CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE, ABS, MAX(.,0) - is already a 4-node live-archive block including this parent's own, and the bare roe-minus-leverage-delta spread measured rho 0.920 against 4cf4ee72. The price normaliser cannot be kept either: dropping only the leverage leg leaves a range-over-price rank, which measured rho 0.824 against the live CS_RANK($roe) - TS_RANK($high - $low, 10), and the parent's own ($high - $low) / (TS_MEAN($open, 42) + 1e-8) is a 9-node subtree. So the range is scaled by pairing it with $return inside a correlation instead: how tightly the day's move tracks the day's range is the same trading-wide-under-stress signal in one node, and the $return basis is what decorrelates it from the volume-vs-range corr legs. Evidence: this exact chassis at window 15 was scored in this run at mean IC 0.00761 and cleared correlation, archive_subtree and coverage, against a 0.00652 floor; corr legs in this archive strengthen with window (0.0070 at 21, 0.0078 at 63), so 42 is the safer horizon. Structurally free: the only archive user of TS_CORR($return, $high - $low, w) is ca6d1041 at w = 21 and it is evicted, while every live 42-day corr leg uses $volume.
